title: Why Can't Cats Taste Sugar? 1 Broken Gene 🐱
description:
Why can't cats taste sweet things? In 2005, scientists found that cats carry a broken copy of the Tas1r2 gene, one half of the sweet taste receptor, so sugar tastes like nothing to them, and lions, tigers and cheetahs share the same broken gene.

topic: Why can't cats taste anything sweet?
script: Your cat can't taste sugar, and one broken gene is why. Put a sweet treat in front of one, and to the cat, it tastes like nothing. To taste sweet, your tongue needs a tiny lock, built from two parts that work as a pair. In 2005, scientists looked inside cat DNA, and found one of those parts was broken. The gene for it is missing 247 letters, so the lock never gets built. No lock, no sweet. And it's not just house cats. Lions, tigers and cheetahs carry the same broken gene. Which honestly makes sense. Cats eat almost nothing but meat, and meat has barely any sugar. So losing sweet cost them nothing at all. So if your cat keeps stealing your ice cream, what do you think it's really after?
key_facts: Sweet taste needs a receptor made of two proteins, T1R2 and T1R3
Cats' Tas1r2 gene is a pseudogene missing 247 base pairs (Li et al., PLoS Genetics, 2005)
Lions, tigers and cheetahs carry the same broken gene
Cats are obligate carnivores and meat has almost no sugar
